correctness.rationale: The Fano-incidence normalization yields 14 vertices and 21 edges. A proof enumerates all graph automorphisms as 168 binary linear maps and polarity times 168, and executable verification checks all their edges. Restricted-growth words enumerate all proper color-class partitions with at most four classes exactly once (1,350,29610 by class count). Checking each of 335 nonidentity automorphisms proves zero successful partitions of size at most three and exactly 13692 successful four-class partitions, giving 328608 labelled colorings. Orbits reconstructed by 336 maps give 51 orbit-size profile {56:1,84:1,112:1,168:16,336:32}. Ten small-palette orbit representatives have concrete nontrivial color-preserving witnesses. A second structurally independent C++ labelled-coloring search finds 0 successful three-colorings and 328608 successful four-colorings, with the same orbit counts. All finite candidates, not a partial sample, are examined.

originality.rationale: The earliest source explicitly defining the invariant is Collins–Trenk (2006), 10.37236/1042. Cranston (2018) already supplies one proper distinguishing four-coloring of Heawood and thus the four-color upper bound; the new contribution is complete exact multiplicity, sharp three-color obstruction classification and 51 inequivalent optimum partitions. Checked general upper-bound literature, the standard chromatic polynomial, and nonproper distinguishing polynomials do not imply those enumerative claims. The prior index returned only neighboring graph/coloring topics. There remains a residual possibility of an unindexed equivalent finite enumeration.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier enumeration of symmetry-breaking proper color-class partitions of the Fano Levi graph, possibly under asymmetry, color-rigidity or graph-labelling terminology, could have matching claims.
A traditional precomputed permutation-group table not indexed in the searched research sources could imply the orbit classification; none was identified or assumed absent.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the canonical cubic girth-six incidence cage with a 336-element automorphism group. Understanding exact optimal proper symmetry-breaking placements is a natural graph-coloring classification, not a generic chosen subslice. Beyond the four-color existence already known, 13692 optimal partitions and their 51 graph-isomorphism orbits quantify every configuration, and three exceptional residual class-permuting symmetry types elucidate the gap between palette-rigidity and unordered partition-rigidity. Reproducible orbit representatives and three-color obstruction witnesses make the classification verifiable and potentially reusable.
